title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 'EZ2' continues a short Eilenberg–Zilber digression inside the notes for the divided-power de Rham lecture. The previous page builds cup products from Eilenberg–Zilber maps. The next page states Dold's theorem: for X a simplicial set, the complexes Hom^·(Z(X^n), ZX^{⊗n}) and Hom^·(ZX^{⊗n}, Z(X^n)), natural in X, are free Σ_n-resolutions of Z.

Step by step:

(1) Equivariant resolution. Σ_n acts freely on EΣ_n, with quotient EΣ_n/Σ_n = K(Σ_n,1). So W_n = Z EΣ_n → Z is a free resolution of Z by Σ_n-modules.

(2) Corollary of the (Dold) theorem. Since the natural Hom complex is also a free resolution of Z, the comparison theorem for projective resolutions gives a Σ_n-map W_n → Hom^·(Z(X×…×X), ZX⊗…⊗ZX). It is unique up to homotopy and natural in X. By adjunction one gets λ: W_n ⊗ Z(X^n) → ZX^{⊗n}. It extends the Alexander–Whitney map and is equivariant up to all higher homotopies. Symmetrically, W_n ⊗ ZX^{⊗n} → Z(X^n) extends the shuffle map. 'Ceci exprime l'homotopie-commutativité': AW is commutative only up to coherent homotopy, and λ packages this. In modern terms, this is the E∞-coalgebra structure on chains, i.e. the E∞-algebra structure on cochains (Barratt–Eccles type).

(3) Topological analogue. For an H-space X with multiplication m: X×X → X:
- homotopy commutativity is a Σ_2-equivariant map I×X×X → X;
- the stronger condition is a Σ_2-map EΣ_2×X^2 → X, with EΣ_2 = lim S^n under the antipodal action and quotients P^n(R);
- more generally, Σ_n-maps EΣ_n×X^n → X lift the iterated multiplication.
The sketch 'x,y: xy=yx, x y x^{-1} y^{-1}' and S^1×X^2 → X ⊂ S^2×X^2 → … shows the successive homotopies on spheres. The top-right diagram goes E(Σ_n≀Σ_j)×X^{nj} → EΣ_n×(EΣ_j)^n×… → EΣ_n×X^n → X, with a '?'. This asks for compatibility of these structure maps under composition, i.e. the operad-algebra axioms (May 1972).

(4) Corollary. If X is such an H-space, ZX gets Σ_n-equivariant maps W_n⊗ZX^{⊗n} → ZX. These induce the Pontryagin product ZX^{⊗n} →(EZ shuffle) Z(X^n) →(Z(m)) ZX.

(5) Steenrod operations (char p coefficients A). Take a cochain f: Z̃X → A[n] representing a class in H^n(X,A). Form
W_p⊗Z(X^p) →(λ) ZX^{⊗p} →(f^{⊗p}) A[n]^{⊗p} →(μ) A[pn],
which is Σ_p-equivariant. Precompose with the diagonal Δ: W_p⊗ZX → W_p⊗Z(X^p), with trivial Σ_p action on ZX. Passing to Σ_p-coinvariants, (W_p⊗ZX)/Σ_p = ZX⊗Z K(Σ_p,1). This gives Pf in H^{pn}(K(Σ_p,1)×X, A), which by Künneth is H^*(Σ_p)⊗_{F_p} H^*(X,A). The coefficients of Pf are the Steenrod powers. This is Steenrod's classical construction (reference 'cf Steenrod … p99').
errors: The equivariant group is written Σ_n in 'H^{pn}_{Σ_n}' and in the coinvariant formula. In the Steenrod construction it should be Σ_p, as the rest of the computation uses.
The Künneth identification H^*(BΣ_p×X, A) ≅ H^*(Σ_p)⊗H^*(X,A) needs A to be (flat over) F_p and finite-type hypotheses. This is implicit but fine.
μ: A^{⊗p} → A is Σ_p-equivariant only because A is commutative. This is not stated.
Pf as written (μ∘f^{⊗p}∘λ) still needs precomposition with Δ to give a class on X. The page indicates Δ by an arrow, so this is a notational gap only.

ideas.what: Natural Σ_n-equivariant map W_n⊗Z(X^n) → ZX^{⊗n} extending Alexander–Whitney, obtained by acyclic models (Dold's theorem): the E∞ structure on chains/cochains
ideas.modern_name: E∞ (Barratt–Eccles / Steenrod cup-i) structure on singular cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod (cup-i, 1947), Dold (1958), May (1970s), Berger–Fresse, McClure–Smith, Mandell

ideas.what: Homotopy-commutative H-spaces with coherent Σ_n-maps EΣ_n×X^n → X, with compatibility under wreath products
ideas.modern_name: E∞-spaces / algebras over the Barratt–Eccles operad
ideas.usually_credited_to: Boardman–Vogt (1968–73), May (Geometry of Iterated Loop Spaces 1972), Barratt–Eccles (1974)
ideas.where_published: Operad-like ideas loosely in Pursuing Stacks (1983); not this form

ideas.what: Construction of Steenrod powers via W_p ⊗ ZX → ZX^{⊗p} → A[pn] and Künneth for BΣ_p×X
ideas.modern_name: Steenrod's construction of reduced power operations

missed.claim: In a lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex, Grothendieck sets the E∞ structure of cochains and the resulting Steenrod operations next to that complex. This suggests he was thinking of comparing divided-power (crystalline / de Rham) structures with E∞-cochain structures and Steenrod operations in char p. That comparison was later developed independently (Mandell's p-adic homotopy theory; Toën and Bhatt–Lurie on cosimplicial / derived divided-power algebras). Nothing on this page develops the link beyond recalling the classical construction.
missed.quote: Constr des opérations de Steenrod: … A un anneau de car p … Pf = μ∘f^{⊗p}∘λ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that by c.1976 Grothendieck connected E∞/Steenrod structure with divided-power de Rham theory. This prefigures the 'schématisation' problem in Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean recollection of classical material: Dold/acyclic models, Steenrod's construction, and E∞ H-spaces. The only mild interest is the context (a divided-power de Rham lecture) and the operadic '?' about wreath-product compatibility. Both are known in the literature (May, Boardman–Vogt).
transcription_corrections: Top line: Grothendieck is relating Σ_n → EΣ_n to K(Σ_n,1) as the quotient. 'Σ_n×Σ_n=Σ_n' is a scribbled side remark (likely about the diagonal Σ_n → Σ_n×Σ_n).

The top-right diagram reads: E(Σ_n≀Σ_j)×(X^1_1…X^1_j)×…×(X^n_1…X^n_j) → EΣ_n×(EΣ_j)^n×X^{nj} (with a crossed-out factor), down to EΣ_n×X^n → X, with a '?'. It is a single diagram, not interleaved with the left-column text.
'Z X^♯' in the corollary should read ZX (target of W_n⊗ZX^{⊗n} → ZX, Σ_n-equivariant, trivial action on the target).
'H^{pn}_{Σ_n}(Z(X^p),A)' and '(W_n⊗ZX)/Σ_n = ZX⊗Z K(Σ_n,1)' are as written, but should be Σ_p.
Reference box reads roughly 'cf Steenrod Coll ops p99' (likely Steenrod's colloquium lectures / Steenrod–Epstein). The exact wording is uncertain.
